query:
title: Go breaking-change review prerequisites

question: An ARM specification change is ready for Go SDK breaking-change review. ARM signoff is still pending, and the author is asking for the Go approval label. What should happen next? Give guidance only; do not approve or change labels.
ground_truth: Explain that ARM signoff and Go SDK compatibility review are separate decisions. Establish the applicable review prerequisites and obtain pending ARM signoff before requesting final Go breaking-change approval. Then have the Go reviewers assess the generated SDK changes. Do not claim to approve or add a label, and do not infer approval from passing validation.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go development-branch suppression is not release approval
query:
title: Go development-branch suppression

question: An ARM specification change targets a development branch for a private preview. Go SDK validation flags breaking changes. The team wants to suppress the gate now and later copy the same changes to a published release branch. Does a development-branch suppression establish release approval?
ground_truth: No. Distinguish the development/private-preview context from a published release and distinguish suppression from compatibility approval. Verify the applicable branch policy and authorized reviewer decision before suppressing a gate. A development-branch exception is not blanket approval for a later release; review the actual release change and generated Go SDK compatibility again as required. Do not apply or promise labels.

query:
title: Go breaking-change label unrelated to my change

question: My specification change only adds an example. The Go SDK comparison also reports a removed exported field. I believe the removal comes from another change. What evidence should I collect before requesting suppression?
ground_truth: Inspect the generated Go diff/changelog and the compared specification versions or commits to establish whether the removal is actually unrelated. Correlate the changed example with the reported removal rather than accepting the author's assertion as proof. Present the finding and applicable suppression process to an authorized reviewer. Do not recommend blanket suppression or changing the comparison baseline arbitrarily.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go operation rename preserves HTTP but breaks callers
query:
title: Go operation rename compatibility

question: The service keeps the same PATCH URI and method, but a TypeSpec operation updateTags is renamed to update. The released Go client exports UpdateTags; regeneration removes it and adds Update. Is the unchanged HTTP contract enough to establish SDK compatibility, and how can I preserve the Go name?
ground_truth: No: removing UpdateTags breaks Go callers even if HTTP behavior is unchanged. Preserve the released Go operation name through a Go-scoped client customization on the underlying TypeSpec operation, for example @@clientName(update, "updateTags", "go") in client.tsp with the appropriate namespace. Regenerate and verify the old Go method remains. ARM/wire compatibility and Go SDK compatibility are independent.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go wire-contract bug fix versus preserved fiction
query:
title: Go boolean property spec correction

question: A response property was incorrectly specified as a string enum, but the deployed service has always returned a JSON boolean. The corrected spec changes the generated Go field from *string to *bool. Would keeping the old string type automatically solve compatibility?
ground_truth: No. Preserving a string type can preserve Go source shape while leaving the client unable to decode the actual boolean response. Distinguish the verified wire-contract correction from the exported Go type change, which still breaks callers. Review affected released clients, consumers, and mitigation with the Go owners; use versioning/customization only when it represents a valid supported contract. Do not assert that a spec bug fix automatically grants Go approval.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Extensible SKU values in TypeSpec

question: An Azure API SKU can gain new string values over time. It is currently modeled as enum Sku { Small, Large }. What TypeSpec shape avoids closing the value set, and does that alone approve the generated Go change?
ground_truth: Use a union with named string literals plus the string scalar, such as union Sku { Small: "Small", Large: "Large", string }. Azure core's no-enum guidance favors extensibility; version enums are a separate allowed use. Review the generated Go API and published compatibility independently. A recommended API shape does not automatically approve an SDK breaking change.

testcase: Go green checks with blocking review comment
query:
title: Go SDK merge readiness

question: A generated Go SDK change has passing required checks and no merge conflict. A reviewer has an unresolved blocking comment about a public field name. Is the change ready to merge, and what should the author do? Assume these facts are given, not live repository status.
ground_truth: It is not ready to merge while the blocking naming comment remains unresolved. Address the naming issue in the appropriate source/customization, regenerate if necessary, and obtain reviewer confirmation. Passing CI and absence of conflicts do not replace review approval. Do not claim to approve or invent a reviewer handle.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Preserve released Go field names

question: A stable Go model exposes ToBsuid and FromBsuid. A specification cleanup regenerates those fields with different casing. The wire property names do not change. Should we accept the new Go names merely because the wire contract is identical?
ground_truth: No. Removing or renaming exported stable fields is a Go source-compatibility change independently of serialization names. Preserve the established Go names with Go-scoped client customizations on the underlying TypeSpec properties, regenerate, and verify the compatibility diff. Do not generalize this to never correcting naming on an unreleased API.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go review handoff without owner identity
query:
title: Go SDK review handoff

question: The generated Go SDK change has passed required checks and all blocking review comments are resolved. I have not supplied requested reviewers or CODEOWNERS. Can you give the final approval or tell me which exact person to ping?
ground_truth: The bot cannot grant approval or claim it has done so. Based on the supplied facts it can identify that a human review/approval handoff remains, but cannot invent a person's name or handle. Direct the author to actual requested reviewers or matching CODEOWNERS, verifying them if the artifact is available. Do not invent additional CI failures.

query:
title: Preserve Go naming customization

question: A reviewer requested a Go acronym-casing correction in a generated SDK. I edited the generated .go file and regeneration overwrote it. How should I make a durable naming fix?
ground_truth: Make the naming customization in the supported specification/client customization layer, using Go-scoped client naming on the relevant TypeSpec symbol where appropriate, instead of only editing generated output. Regenerate and inspect the resulting Go symbol and compatibility diff. Preserve already released public names; a new naming preference is not grounds to rename stable APIs without review.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Go generation cannot find serialized type field

question: SDK generation fails with "field with serializedName 'type' not found in model 'ArmConnectionResponse'" while processing a response example. The TypeSpec model inherits from a tracked ARM resource. I have not supplied emitted Swagger or the full example. Can you identify the fix?
ground_truth: Explain that the diagnostic is an example/model serialization mismatch requiring inspection of the actual emitted model and the referenced example. Compare the response shape, inherited fields, visibility and generator/version context before deciding the correction. Ask for the necessary emitted model/example/log details or show how to obtain generation artifacts. Do not assert a specific decorator or deletion fixes it based only on inheritance.

expected_references.title: SDK validation artifacts and detailed errors

query:
title: Go SDK validation repository checkout failure

question: The log says "failed to get sdk repo: core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig" and then "Failed to read generateOutput.json". Multiple unrelated services fail with this same checkout error. Should I change my API model to fix it?
ground_truth: The primary failure is repository/Git checkout tooling, not evidence of an API model defect. The missing generateOutput.json is likely downstream of checkout failure. Collect the detailed run/log context, check for a shared automation incident or Git compatibility issue, and escalate to engineering-system owners. Retry after the actual infrastructure fix; do not prescribe arbitrary spec changes or claim a historical incident is the current cause.

expected_references.title: SDK validation artifacts and detailed errors

testcase: Go APIView name versus revision approval
query:
title: Go APIView revision blocks release

question: The package name is already marked First Release Approved. The SDK change merged, but the release check reports that the newly generated GA APIView revision lacks API approval. Does the existing package-name approval satisfy that gate?
ground_truth: No. Package-name/first-release approval and API approval of the exact revision are different gates. Request the authorized API reviewer to inspect and approve the revision the release pipeline references, after resolving its blocking comments. PR merge or an earlier revision's approval is not proof this revision is approved. The bot must not claim to approve it.

testcase: Go release success needs registry evidence
query:
title: Go package publication verification

question: A release pipeline has been triggered for a Go module, but I have not supplied its run result or evidence that the requested version is in the Go module registry. Can you conclude the package was released?
ground_truth: No. A triggered run or pipeline definition proves neither successful completion nor package publication. Verify the matching module/version and successful release run separately, then confirm availability through the Go module ecosystem, such as go get module@version and the corresponding pkg.go.dev version. State publication remains unknown without that evidence; do not offer to trigger a release from this read-only bot.

query:
title: Go dependency allowlist exception

question: A new Go SDK module would depend on a native binary distribution module outside azure-sdk-for-go. The current repository dependency instruction does not list it. The team proposes adding an exception. Is the proposal itself permission to merge?
ground_truth: No. Check the actual repository go.mod dependency policy and the proposed module's requirements; an unapproved exception is not existing policy. Obtain owner review of the dependency and the policy change, including applicable compatibility and maintenance concerns. Do not claim all external dependencies are prohibited or invent an approved exception.

testcase: Go module deprecation versus immediate deletion
query:
title: Deprecating a Go SDK module

question: A service is retiring and its Go SDK module has no replacement. Can we immediately delete the module instead of publishing a deprecation notice? What should the deprecation change contain?
ground_truth: Distinguish deprecation from deletion and retraction. Follow the applicable lifecycle policy and publish the appropriate final patch with a Deprecated module comment in go.mod, changelog notice, and README guidance. If there is no replacement, state that honestly rather than inventing migration to another module. Removal timing needs the applicable policy and owner review; retirement alone does not establish immediate deletion eligibility.

testcase: Go spec merge does not prove SDK release
query:
title: New API version available to Go consumers

question: Our ARM specification change for a new API version merged. We have not generated or released the Go SDK yet. Can customers consume the new API through the existing Go module just because the specification merged?
ground_truth: A spec merge is not evidence of an updated published Go SDK. Follow the management-plane SDK generation, validation, review and release process for the desired version, then verify publication. Recommend the Azure SDK Tools Agent as the primary lifecycle workflow where applicable, without implying this read-only chatbot can execute it. Do not claim generation/release automatically occurred on merge.

testcase: Go language feature does not prove minimum version policy
query:
title: Raising a Go SDK minimum language version

question: We want generic methods in a new major version of a Go SDK. Someone says a future Go release supports them, so we should raise go.mod's minimum version and drop older consumers. Does that establish an approved compatibility policy?
ground_truth: No. Verify authoritative Go language/release documentation for the exact feature and supported compiler version rather than assuming the proposal shipped. Separately assess module compatibility, supported consumers, and SDK owner approval for a minimum-version change. Do not invent a future Go version or treat one owner's case-specific acceptance as a universal SDK policy.
